purpose: Implement the promoted HRM research decisions incrementally without weakening Hub authority, container isolation, source grounding, or existing APIs.
goal: Deliver a default-disabled, secure HRM experiment domain beginning with a bounded Sudoku vertical slice and ending with evidence-gated release readiness.

milestones.title: Secure data and bounded Sudoku runtime

tasks.title: Add the feature-flagged HRM control-plane domain and closed contracts
acceptance_criteria: A default-disabled HRM domain exposes narrow Hub-side ports for admission, persistence, dispatch, events, artifacts and evaluation without changing existing LoRA or chat contracts.
Hub-owned IDs, tenant/project scope, idempotency, CAS/lease fencing and fail-closed policy checks are represented by closed request/result contracts.
Workers cannot create queue entries, select other workers, project authoritative Hub status or communicate worker-to-worker.
Focused contract and service tests cover disabled mode, scope isolation, stale revision, unknown fields and replay behavior.

tasks.title: Build the pinned and isolated HRM worker runtime boundary
acceptance_criteria: The HRM worker runs in its own non-root container with read-only root, cap-drop-all, no-new-privileges, bounded tmpfs/workspace and no Docker socket or host namespace access.
Dependencies and base images are digest/version pinned with deterministic build metadata; network and telemetry are denied by default.
Execution is assignment-, WorkerJob-, dispatch-lease-, attempt-, deadline- and digest-bound with process-group cancellation and bounded cleanup.
Preflight denies missing isolation, incompatible hardware/runtime and stale or widened authority with stable reason codes.

tasks.title: Implement secure dataset, checkpoint and artifact admission
acceptance_criteria: Dataset and checkpoint manifests bind scope, digest, byte size, schema, license state and provenance before visibility or execution.
Checkpoint admission is safetensors-only; pickle, torch.load, custom classes, dynamic imports, object hooks and trust_remote_code are denied.
Archive traversal, links, bombs, tenant/path escape, SSRF, redirect/DNS rebinding and unbounded streams fail closed.
Artifact publication crosses the Worker boundary only through verified relative paths, size/hash checks and current dispatch leases.

tasks.title: Deliver the bounded Sudoku end-to-end vertical slice
acceptance_criteria: The Hub can admit, dispatch, observe, cancel, reconcile and accept one bounded Sudoku experiment through the existing task/WorkerJob control plane.
The deterministic 9x9 fixture validator enforces shape, range, givens, rows, columns, boxes and canonical solution equality.
Events are monotonic, paginated and integrity-bound; retry, cancel/result races and stale ingress have deterministic tests.
Mock and contract profiles pass locally while CPU/GPU performance and accuracy remain unclaimed without their own RUN evidence.

tasks.title: Add independently gated Maze and ARC puzzle plugins
acceptance_criteria: Maze and ARC use separate narrow codec, normalizer and validator ports and cannot dynamically load untrusted plugin code.
Maze defines bounded grids, start/goal, obstacles, path validity, shortest-path semantics and unsolvable cases.
ARC defines bounded colors/grids, train/test structure, output validation, license state and egress suitability.
Either plugin may remain disabled or deferred without blocking the Sudoku domain.

tasks.title: Expose evaluation, reports and consistent Hub client surfaces
acceptance_criteria: Hub APIs implement the published HRM OpenAPI contract with stable pagination, sorting, idempotency, authorization and error codes.
Evaluation and offline comparison reports preserve dataset/checkpoint/run provenance and never infer accuracy from documentation.
Angular, Visual Process, TUI and CLI use only Hub IDs and APIs and expose no Worker URLs, server paths or local checkpoint paths.
The UI is explicitly experimental, accessible and bounded for loading, empty, error, cancel and stale-event states.

tasks.title: Close adversarial, compatibility and experimental release gates
acceptance_criteria: Contract, security, tenant-isolation, replay, cancellation, recovery and backward-compatibility gates pass with stable audit artifacts.
Any CPU, GPU, performance, accuracy, checkpoint-portability or remote-provider claim is backed by an explicitly approved assignment-bound RUN reference.
Critical and high threat-register entries have verified deny/mitigate controls and named owners; unresolved evidence remains release-blocking.
The experimental feature remains default-disabled and requires an explicit Hub approval for release enablement.

summary_notes: All 32 HRM research decision IDs are mapped exactly once across the seven implementation tasks.
The Track is passive until separate Hub adoption and materialization transitions succeed.
Runtime, GPU, performance and accuracy are not claimed by this plan.
Adoption requires an approval decision by a canonical principal distinct from the Hub actor that derived this Track revision.
